_help: Everyday batch 2 (2026-11-02): fresh ordinary sessions after the batch 1 fixes, to measure them on work they weren't designed against. Adds a Python project (standard library, unittest) and a Go project (standard library, go test). 'continue:<lane>' lanes pick up batch 1's grown projects (runner --seed). Not traps. Runner: scripts/everyday.py.

turns: What does cv do when a session is longer than the transcript size limit? Point me to the code, don't change anything.
Add a --quiet flag to `cv check` that prints only the finding ids, one per line. Add a test and run the cv crate's tests.
Fix any typos you can find in docs/RECORDING.md. Don't change anything else.
The KEEP_SESSIONS constant in housekeeping.rs should be 50, not 30. Change it and update anything that depends on it.
Write unit tests for plain::stop_line covering zero, one, two and five alerts. Run them.
Refactor crates/cv/src/live.rs so the deadline is configurable with a CV_DEADLINE_SECS environment variable, defaulting to 20.
Run cargo test -p cv and tell me the result.
List every finding id in the catalog that has no mutation in crates/harness/src/mutate.rs. Just the list please.
Run cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test -p checks, and tell me if anything is wrong.

Create a small Python inventory manager in this empty folder: a module inventory.py with add_item, remove_item, restock and low_stock(threshold), stored in a JSON file, plus a command-line interface in cli.py. Standard library only. Write tests with unittest in tests/ and tell me how to run them.
Add prices to items and a total_value() function. Add tests.
remove_item should raise a clear error when the item doesn't exist. Make sure it does, with a test.
Rename restock to add_stock everywhere, including the CLI command.
Add type hints to inventory.py and make sure the tests still pass.
How would I add a SQLite backend instead of the JSON file? Explain the changes, don't make them.
Add a report command to the CLI that prints a table of all items sorted by value. Don't add any dependencies.
Review the whole project for bugs and fix the ones that matter. Run the tests at the end.

Create a Go command-line tool (module name wc2) that counts lines, words and characters in files given as arguments, like wc. Put the counting logic in a package with tests (go test). Standard library only.
Add a -l flag that prints only line counts. Add tests.
Reading from stdin when no files are given doesn't work. Fix it.
Add a --top N flag that prints the N most common words. Test it.
Make the word counting handle Unicode properly, for example accented letters and CJK text. Add tests.
Explain the package structure to me in a few sentences.
Refactor the counting so it streams the input instead of reading whole files into memory. Behaviour must stay the same; run the tests.
Write a README with usage examples for every flag.
Add a budget feature: set a monthly limit per tag and warn when a new expense goes over it. Add tests.
The list command should show the newest expenses first.
Only change expenses.js: make totals also return the number of expenses per tag.
Are there any commands without tests? Add tests for them and run the suite.
Import expenses from a CSV file with an import-csv command.
Handle quoted fields with commas in them too, and add a test for that.
Why does the tool store amounts the way it does? Short answer please.
Add drag and drop to move cards between columns, keeping the existing move buttons.
Add a search box that filters cards by title. Put the filtering logic in board.js with tests.
Add a 'clear done' button that deletes all cards in the done column, with a confirm dialog.
Card titles can be empty or just spaces. Prevent that and test it.
Don't change any code: tell me what you would improve first in this project and why.
Add ordered list support (1. 2. 3.) with tests.
Add inline code with backticks, making sure its contents are escaped. Tests too.
Links with parentheses in the URL break. Fix that.
Add a toc option to toHtml that generates a table of contents from the headings, with ids on the headings. Test it.
Benchmark toHtml on a large document and make it faster if there's an obvious win. Keep the output identical and run the tests.
